rationale: C923 (#923): the member-level interface-implementation contract. Before this fixture the lane published NO edge between a member and the interface member it satisfies, in either form — and C# requires no keyword to satisfy an interface, so the `override`-modifier machinery could not see either one. The fixture is authored against the family's five-lane precedent for the label (`overrides M -> I.m`, measured in java/kotlin/typescript/dart/python by script/m14/tmp/c923-family-member-edge-probe.ts): IMPLICIT (`Implicit : IThingEx`, no keyword written) and EXPLICIT (`void IThing.Reset()`, the interface written in the declaration — published even when the interface is not declared anywhere, `IExternalThing`). CHAIN crosses an interface's own base list (IThingEx : IThing), which is why the ancestor lookup had to be fixed to see a raw-named base (measured gap: Chain.GetName was missing while Chain.Extra was present). HIDDEN pins the refusal a base class's own implementation creates (`new`-hidden member does not claim the slot), UNRELATED pins that a same-named member of a type implementing nothing never licenses an edge even when the interface is declared in the same file, EXTERNAL pins the unknowable-contract refusal for the implicit form, and HELPER pins that an unrelated member of a CONFORMING type publishes nothing. Events appear in all three forms (field-like implicit, field-like hidden/implementing, and the accessor form, which is the only explicit-event form C# allows) because the first run of this fixture exposed that neither event branch collected a contract at all.

forbidRelationships.note: name matching alone: the type implements nothing, and the very interface declaring GetName is in this file — the fabrication the contract must never produce
the same refusal for the void member
the base class Middle already fills the slot; a `new`-hidden member is not the interface implementation
no interface declares Helper — a member of a CONFORMING type is still not an implementation
implicit form against an interface the file never declares: the contract is unknowable here, so the honest answer is no edge

THE OWNER-QUALIFIED SPELLING OF THE SAME REFUSAL, and the pin that kills the surviving mutant csharp/interface-member-conforming-dropped (2026-10-21): that mutant re-adds the C923 over-reach rows with the target spelled `IThing.GetName` instead of `GetName`, and the bare-spelling forbids above cannot see it - so the fabrication was invisible and the mutant SURVIVED the whole battery. The pre-C923 analyzer spelled this row exactly this way, so the spelling is the defect's own signature, not an invented one.
the same owner-qualified spelling of the void-member refusal
the owner-qualified spelling of the base-class-fills-the-slot refusal

THE TARGET-SPELLING CONTRACT, pinned on a CONFORMING member: the interface-implementation edge names the DECLARED MEMBER (`GetName`), never the owner-qualified member (`IThing.GetName`) - the fleet-wide 'the target is the DECLARED MEMBER, not Owner.member' fix (45b879423). A conforming member may have ONE such edge, in ONE spelling.
